1. Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the 30-day window — adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for the first 10 days.

2. Model shows strong upward trend bias after sharp price spikes — reduce forecast slope after a 10+ point spike in history.

3. Model fails to capture mean reversion in the final 5–7 days — add a downward correction of 1–3% for the last 7 days if true outcome shows declining trend.

4. Forecast lags true outcome by 1–3 days — shift forecast 1–3 days ahead to align with observed price momentum.

5. Model overestimates volatility in low-price regimes — reduce forecast by 1–3% when history shows prices below 65.00.

6. Model exhibits “overshoot” after price corrections — cap forecast at 5% above previous day’s true value to avoid overcorrection.
